title: Ingress / Gateway
description: Istio Gateway API gateways public (192.168.68.240) and mcp (192.168.68.241): traffic, errors, latency per backend and host, upstream health, TLS/certificate, mcp JWT authorization, proxy health. Curated for this lab; see docs/dashboards/networking.md.

list.name: Firing alerts
list.expr: ALERTS{alertstate="firing", namespace=~"gateway|istio-system"} or ALERTS{alertstate="firing", alertname=~"Certificate.*", name="wildcard"}

list.name: Gateway listener config pushed
list.textFormat: {{pod}} received new listener config from istiod

panels.title: How to read this dashboard
panels.description: Reading guide for this dashboard.

options.content:
**What this is.** Every HTTPS request from the LAN to `*.staffops.space` enters through an Istio **Gateway**:
`public` (192.168.68.240, all apps) or `mcp` (192.168.68.241, only `mcp.staffops.space`, Keycloak JWT required).
Each Gateway is an Envoy Deployment in namespace `gateway` (`public-istio`, `mcp-istio`), reachable thanks to a MetalLB IP,
terminating TLS with the wildcard certificate from cert-manager and routing by HTTPRoute to the app's Service.

**Healthy looks like:** both gateways UP, success rate (non-5xx) at 100%, p95 latency in the tens/hundreds of ms, no Envoy
response flags other than occasional `DC`/`DR` (client went away), certificate with > 30 days left.

**When something goes red:**
- *5xx for one backend* → check that app (pods, logs); `UH`/`UF` flags mean Envoy found no healthy endpoint / could not connect.
- *5xx for every backend* → gateway itself: pod status, `istioctl proxy-status`, config rejected panel, istiod (Mesh dashboard).
- *401/403 on `mcp`* → JWT missing/invalid or user not in `/mcp/*` group (RBAC panel).
- *Certificate < 14 days* → cert-manager renewal failing (`kubectl --context k8s01 -n gateway describe certificate wildcard`).

Prometheus metrics have no hostname label: traffic is split by **backend Service** (one per hostname here). The *Access logs*
row uses the gateway JSON access log in Loki, which has the real `authority` (host) and `route_name`.
Panels marked *pending scrape* fill after the Envoy stats change is deployed. Details: `docs/dashboards/networking.md`.

panels.title: Active alerts for this service
panels.description: Prometheus alerts of this service that are FIRING (condition true for longer than the rule's `for`) or PENDING (condition true, waiting for `for`). Same filter as the red alert annotations of this dashboard; Watchdog/InfoInhibitor are excluded. Empty = healthy. Alertmanager has no receiver in this lab, so dashboards are where alerts are seen: the rule, its threshold and source are in the rule files (helm-charts/<app>/**/prometheus.rules.yaml or the -raw release) and in docs/dashboards/. All alerts of the lab: dashboard "Alerts overview" (Observability folder).

targets.expr: ALERTS{alertname!~"Watchdog|InfoInhibitor", alertstate=~"firing|pending", namespace=~"gateway|istio-system"} or ALERTS{alertname!~"Watchdog|InfoInhibitor", alertstate=~"firing|pending", alertname=~"Certificate.*", name="wildcard"}

panels.title: Gateway pods
panels.description: Is each gateway Envoy scraped and alive? `up` of the PodMonitor gateway-envoy (job istio-system/gateway-envoy). DOWN means Prometheus cannot reach the pod: the gateway is probably down and its hostnames are unreachable.

panels.title: Requests/s
panels.description: Requests per second through the selected gateways (all backends). Formula from the Istio Mesh dashboard (https://github.com/istio/istio/blob/1.30.8/manifests/addons/dashboards/istio-mesh.libsonnet): sum(rate(istio_requests_total)). Only requests that reached a backend are counted (the http→https 301 redirect is not).

panels.title: Success rate (non-5xx)
panels.description: Share of requests not answered with 5xx. Formula and thresholds from the Istio Mesh dashboard (https://github.com/istio/istio/blob/1.30.8/manifests/addons/dashboards/istio-mesh.libsonnet): red < 95%, yellow < 100%. 4xx count as success (client errors such as 401 without a token).

panels.title: 5xx/s
panels.description: Server errors per second (response_code 5xx) seen by the gateways (https://istio.io/latest/docs/reference/config/metrics/). 0 is normal.

panels.title: p95 latency
panels.description: 95th percentile of request duration (gateway → backend → gateway, ms), all backends. histogram_quantile over istio_request_duration_milliseconds_bucket as in the Istio Mesh dashboard (https://github.com/istio/istio/blob/1.30.8/manifests/addons/dashboards/istio-mesh.libsonnet).

panels.title: Wildcard cert: days left
panels.description: Days until *.staffops.space expires (certmanager_certificate_expiration_timestamp_seconds, https://cert-manager.io/docs/devops-tips/prometheus-metrics/). Let's Encrypt certs last 90 days and cert-manager renews 30 days before expiry, so it should stay between 30 and 90. Red under 14 days = alert CertificateExpiringSoon (helm-charts/cert-manager).

panels.title: LoadBalancer IP
panels.description: IP that MetalLB gave each gateway Service (kube-state-metrics kube_service_status_load_balancer_ingress). Expected: public-istio 192.168.68.240, mcp-istio 192.168.68.241. Missing = Service pending, hostnames unreachable.

panels.title: Certificate ready
panels.description: cert-manager Ready condition of Certificate gateway/wildcard (https://cert-manager.io/docs/devops-tips/prometheus-metrics/). Not ready = alert CertificateNotReady.

panels.title: Next renewal
panels.description: When cert-manager will renew the wildcard certificate (certmanager_certificate_renewal_timestamp_seconds, https://cert-manager.io/docs/devops-tips/prometheus-metrics/).

panels.title: Active downstream connections
panels.description: Open client connections per gateway (envoy_server_total_connections, https://www.envoyproxy.io/docs/envoy/latest/configuration/observability/statistics). Browsers keep HTTP/2 connections open, so a handful is normal; a sudden jump to hundreds is a client storm.

panels.title: Config rejected by Envoy (range)
panels.description: xDS updates (clusters CDS + listeners LDS) that Envoy refused in the time range (https://www.envoyproxy.io/docs/envoy/latest/configuration/upstream/cluster_manager/cds#statistics, https://www.envoyproxy.io/docs/envoy/latest/configuration/listeners/lds#statistics). Anything > 0 means istiod sent config the proxy could not apply: routes may be stale. Check `istioctl proxy-status` and istiod logs.

panels.title: Requests/s by gateway and status code
panels.description: Request rate per gateway and HTTP status code (https://istio.io/latest/docs/reference/config/metrics/). Normal: mostly 2xx/3xx; 401/403 on mcp-istio are clients without a valid token. code 0 = no response was sent (client reset, see flags).

panels.title: Requests/s by backend
panels.description: Request rate per destination Service (≈ per hostname). Which app is getting traffic? (https://istio.io/latest/docs/reference/config/metrics/)

panels.title: 5xx ratio by backend
panels.description: Share of 5xx answers per backend. Same formula as the Istio Mesh/Service dashboards' success rate inverted (https://github.com/istio/istio/blob/1.30.8/manifests/addons/dashboards/istio-mesh.libsonnet); red line at 5% mirrors their red < 95% success threshold. A single backend high = that app; every backend high = the gateway or the node.

targets.expr: sum by (destination_service_name) (rate(istio_requests_total{job="istio-system/gateway-envoy", source_workload=~"$gateway", response_code=~"5.."}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (destination_service_name) (rate(istio_requests_total{job="istio-system/gateway-envoy", source_workload=~"$gateway"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: 4xx/s by backend and code
panels.description: Client errors per backend and code (https://istio.io/latest/docs/reference/config/metrics/). 401/403 on MCP backends = JWT/group checks of the mcp Gateway; 404 = wrong path; 400 bursts on Keycloak usually mean expired login sessions. Not an outage by itself.

panels.title: p95 latency by backend
panels.description: 95th percentile request duration per backend (ms), histogram_quantile over istio_request_duration_milliseconds_bucket (https://github.com/istio/istio/blob/1.30.8/manifests/addons/dashboards/istio-mesh.libsonnet). Compare against the app's normal: Argo CD UI and Keycloak are slower (hundreds of ms) than Vault/Grafana API calls. Long-poll/streaming endpoints inflate it.

panels.title: Backends summary (time range)
panels.description: Per backend over the whole time range: requests, success rate (non-5xx) and p95 latency. Like the 'HTTP/gRPC Workloads' table of the Istio Mesh dashboard (https://github.com/istio/istio/blob/1.30.8/manifests/addons/dashboards/istio-mesh.libsonnet), same success thresholds.

targets.expr: sum by (destination_service_namespace, destination_service_name) (increase(istio_requests_total{job="istio-system/gateway-envoy", source_workload=~"$gateway", response_code!~"5.."}[$__range])) / sum by (destination_service_namespace, destination_service_name) (increase(istio_requests_total{job="istio-system/gateway-envoy", source_workload=~"$gateway"}[$__range]))

histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, destination_service_namespace, destination_service_name) (increase(istio_request_duration_milliseconds_bucket{job="istio-system/gateway-envoy", source_workload=~"$gateway"}[$__range])))

panels.title: Envoy response flags by backend
panels.description: Requests that Envoy tagged with a response flag (https://www.envoyproxy.io/docs/envoy/latest/configuration/observability/access_log/usage#config-access-log-format-response-flags). Key flags: **UH** no healthy upstream (no ready pod), **UF** upstream connection failure, **UT** upstream timeout, **URX** retry limit hit, **NR** no route, **UC/UR** upstream closed/reset, **DC/DR** client disconnected/reset (usually harmless: browser closed a tab). Any U* flag for a backend means the app side is failing.

panels.title: Healthy endpoints of routed backends
panels.description: Healthy endpoints (ready pods) Envoy knows for each backend that received gateway traffic in the last hour (envoy_cluster_membership_healthy, https://www.envoyproxy.io/docs/envoy/latest/configuration/upstream/cluster_manager/cluster_stats; the cluster name outbound|port||<service> is mapped to the Service and joined with istio_requests_total so the ~150 clusters of unrouted Services stay out). 0 → requests fail with 503 UH. **Pending scrape**: this stat only exists once the istiod `meshConfig.defaultConfig.proxyStatsMatcher` change (helm-charts/istio/istiod) is synced and the gateway Deployments are restarted (https://istio.io/latest/docs/ops/configuration/telemetry/envoy-stats/).

targets.expr: label_replace(sum by (cluster_name) (envoy_cluster_membership_healthy{job="istio-system/gateway-envoy", pod=~"($gateway)-.*", cluster_name=~"outbound.*"}), "destination_service", "$1", "cluster_name", "outbound\\|[0-9]+\\|[^|]*\\|(.+)") and on (destination_service) sum by (destination_service) (increase(istio_requests_total{job="istio-system/gateway-envoy", source_workload=~"$gateway"}[1h])) > 0

panels.title: Upstream connect failures & timeouts
panels.description: Failed or timed-out TCP connections from the gateway to backend pods (envoy_cluster_upstream_cx_connect_fail / _connect_timeout, https://www.envoyproxy.io/docs/envoy/latest/configuration/upstream/cluster_manager/cluster_stats). Should be 0; > 0 means pods crash, refuse connections or a NetworkPolicy blocks the gateway. **Pending scrape**: this stat only exists once the istiod `meshConfig.defaultConfig.proxyStatsMatcher` change (helm-charts/istio/istiod) is synced and the gateway Deployments are restarted (https://istio.io/latest/docs/ops/configuration/telemetry/envoy-stats/).

panels.title: Upstream request timeouts, retries & overflow
panels.description: Requests that hit the route timeout (upstream_rq_timeout), were retried (upstream_rq_retry), or were rejected by the circuit breaker (upstream_rq_pending_overflow) (https://www.envoyproxy.io/docs/envoy/latest/configuration/upstream/cluster_manager/cluster_stats). All 0 normally; timeouts point at a slow backend, overflow at a backend that cannot keep up. **Pending scrape**: this stat only exists once the istiod `meshConfig.defaultConfig.proxyStatsMatcher` change (helm-charts/istio/istiod) is synced and the gateway Deployments are restarted (https://istio.io/latest/docs/ops/configuration/telemetry/envoy-stats/).

panels.title: TLS handshakes and errors
panels.description: Successful TLS handshakes vs TLS connection errors on the HTTPS listeners (listener ssl.handshake / ssl.connection_error, https://www.envoyproxy.io/docs/envoy/latest/configuration/listeners/stats — TLS statistics). Errors without handshakes = clients that don't trust the cert, speak plain HTTP to 443, or ask for an unknown SNI. **Pending scrape**: this stat only exists once the istiod `meshConfig.defaultConfig.proxyStatsMatcher` change (helm-charts/istio/istiod) is synced and the gateway Deployments are restarted (https://istio.io/latest/docs/ops/configuration/telemetry/envoy-stats/).

panels.title: Downstream connections per gateway
panels.description: Open client connections per gateway pod (envoy_server_total_connections, https://www.envoyproxy.io/docs/envoy/latest/configuration/observability/statistics). Each LAN client with HTTP/2 keeps one or a few. Overflow (listener downstream_cx_overflow) is not configured here.

panels.title: RBAC decisions on mcp
panels.description: Envoy RBAC filter results on the mcp Gateway (envoy_http_rbac, https://www.envoyproxy.io/docs/envoy/latest/configuration/http/http_filters/rbac_filter#statistics): **allowed** passed both AuthorizationPolicies (valid JWT + /mcp/admin or /mcp/viewer group), **denied** were rejected with 403. Requests with an invalid token are rejected earlier with 401 by the JWT filter (see the 4xx panel). A burst of denied = a client lost its group or is misconfigured.

panels.title: 401/403 on mcp by backend
panels.description: Requests refused on the mcp Gateway per MCP server: 401 = missing/invalid JWT, 403 = valid JWT without an /mcp/* group (https://istio.io/latest/docs/reference/config/metrics/).

panels.title: Requests by host
panels.description: Requests per hostname (authority) from the gateway JSON access log (meshConfig.accessLogEncoding JSON). LogQL count_over_time on json-parsed lines (https://grafana.com/docs/loki/latest/query/metric_queries/). Includes 301 redirects on port 80.

panels.title: p95 duration by host
panels.description: 95th percentile of the access-log `duration` field (ms) per hostname, LogQL quantile_over_time with unwrap (https://grafana.com/docs/loki/latest/query/metric_queries/). Same idea as the Prometheus latency panel but split by host instead of backend Service.

targets.expr: quantile_over_time(0.95, {k8s_namespace_name="gateway", k8s_container_name="istio-proxy", k8s_deployment_name=~"$gateway"} |= "response_code" | json | __error__="" | unwrap duration [$__auto]) by (authority)

panels.title: Errors by host / route (time range)
panels.description: Count of access-log lines with status ≥ 500 or a response flag over the time range, grouped by host, HTTPRoute rule (route_name = namespace.route.rule), status and flag (https://www.envoyproxy.io/docs/envoy/latest/configuration/observability/access_log/usage#config-access-log-format-response-flags). Start here to find *which* route fails.

targets.expr: sum by (authority, route_name, response_code, response_flags) (count_over_time({k8s_namespace_name="gateway", k8s_container_name="istio-proxy", k8s_deployment_name=~"$gateway"} |= "response_code" | json | __error__="" | response_code >= 500 or response_flags != "-" [$__range]))

panels.title: Recent failing requests
panels.description: Raw access-log lines with status ≥ 500 or a response flag (newest first). Fields: authority (host), path, response_code, response_flags (https://www.envoyproxy.io/docs/envoy/latest/configuration/observability/access_log/usage#config-access-log-format-response-flags), upstream_host (backend pod), duration (ms), upstream_transport_failure_reason.

targets.expr: {k8s_namespace_name="gateway", k8s_container_name="istio-proxy", k8s_deployment_name=~"$gateway"} |= "response_code" | json | __error__="" | response_code >= 500 or response_flags != "-"

panels.title: xDS connection to istiod
panels.description: Each gateway keeps one gRPC connection to istiod to receive config (envoy_cluster_upstream_cx_active for cluster xds-grpc, as in the Istio Control Plane dashboard). 0 = the gateway runs on its last config and won't see new routes/endpoints.

panels.title: Config updates applied
panels.description: Successful listener (LDS) and cluster (CDS) updates per gateway (https://www.envoyproxy.io/docs/envoy/latest/configuration/listeners/lds#statistics, https://www.envoyproxy.io/docs/envoy/latest/configuration/upstream/cluster_manager/cds#statistics). Steps follow HTTPRoute/Service changes; constant churn means something keeps changing config.

panels.title: Gateway memory & CPU
panels.description: Working-set memory (left) and CPU cores (right) of each gateway's istio-proxy container (cAdvisor). Envoy grows with the number of routes/clusters; a steady climb with flat traffic is a leak.
